objects.text: How one family turned a 1940s Kochi bungalow into a calm, bright home.
objects.name: Body

objects.text: When Maya and Joseph first saw the house, the roof leaked and the garden was a jungle. Two years later, it is the calmest place they know.
objects.name: Article text

objects.text: They kept the old teak beams and red oxide floors, opened the rooms to the courtyard and painted every wall a soft warm white.
objects.name: Article text

objects.text: The kitchen moved to the back of the house, next to the garden, so mornings now start with filter coffee among the banana plants.
objects.name: Article text

objects.text: 'We didn't want a showroom,' says Maya. 'We wanted a home that gets better as it gets older.'
objects.name: Article text

objects.text: Teak, terracotta and a lot of sunlight: the bungalow after two years of careful work.
